McLaren.summary: McLaren has tweaked the front and rear corners of the car’s aerodynamics and introduced a fresh diffuser shape, all aimed at smoothing the airflow around the car. The changes should give a tighter, more stable front end and extra rear‑end grip, letting the drivers carry more speed through the corners this weekend. In short, better airflow = better handling, and that could translate into a stronger qualifying and race performance.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull’s new front wing now sports an extra little vane on the lower edge of the endplate, which helps keep the airflow clean and gives the car a bit more front‑end grip. At the front corners they’ve tweaked the flexible rubber strip that seals the wheel‑rim area, improving durability so the car can stay on the optimal tyre‑temperature window longer. Together, these tweaks should translate into steadier handling on the straights and through the first turns, giving the team a better chance to extract maximum performance this weekend.

Scuderia Ferrari.summary: Ferrari’s new floor and diffuser package reshapes the front‑floor edge, adds extra volume to the side‑pod inlets and tweaks the rear diffuser’s shape, all to smooth airflow and boost down‑force. The changes should give the car better grip through the high‑speed corners of this weekend’s circuit, letting the drivers carry more speed and fight harder for positions.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls have refreshed a host of aero pieces for the weekend – a new end‑plate on the front wing, extra flap bits on the rear wing and a reshaped engine‑cover shoulder – all aimed at smoothing the airflow and giving the car a cleaner rear‑end. The floor gets a complete makeover, with fresh leading‑edge devices, a revised board and edge, plus a brand‑new front brake‑duct and floor board to boost down‑force where it counts. In short, the tweaks should improve grip and stability through the corners, helping the RB drivers extract more speed without having to fight the car’s balance.

Alpine F1 Team.summary: Alpine has tweaked the back of the car – the rear‑floor corner has been reshaped and the rear‑wing flap has a new profile. These changes give the car a bit more grip and stability, especially in high‑speed corners, so the drivers can push harder and defend better this weekend. In short, the updates should translate into quicker lap times and more confidence when battling on track.

Cadillac.summary: Cadillac has tweaked the shape of the forward floor fences to smooth the airflow under the car, giving it a little extra down‑force and stability in the fast corners. They’ve also reshaped the side‑pod cooling vents on the roof to keep the power unit running cooler without sacrificing grip. Together, the changes should help the car stay glued to the track and maintain peak performance throughout the weekend’s sprint and main race.
